title: Relief
text:
Methodology
The methodology was set by the project lead and is binding:

Polygon statistics only. Every statistic comes from the whole parcel polygon via exactextractr::exact_extract(), each pixel weighted by the share of it inside the parcel; never from the centroid or from pixel centres.
Aspect is measured clockwise from north, in degrees.
Flat pixels. A pixel with a slope below flat_slope_deg (0.5° in 00-setup.R) contributes 0 to both aspect variables, since its aspect is meaningless.
Metric distances. Slope and aspect are computed with distances in metres or with a geodesic-aware method; never with degrees treated as metres, and never in Web Mercator.
Small parcels. A parcel smaller than one pixel still gets values.
Complete output. Every parcel gets a value for every variable.


Steps

Crop. crop(rast("data/interim/dem.vrt"), <parcels' extent + 0.02°>). The margin gives terrain() neighbouring pixels at the edge of every parcel. The DEM stays in EPSG:4326 and is never resampled or reprojected.
Slope and aspect. terrain(dem, c("slope", "aspect"), unit = "degrees"). For longitude/latitude data, terra computes the cell distances needed for slope and aspect on the WGS 84 ellipsoid (from ?terra::terrain: “Distances (needed for slope and aspect) for longitude/latitude data are computed on the WGS84 ellipsoid with Karney’s algorithm”). So no degree is treated as a metre.
Aspect encoding. Aspect is a circular angle: 359° and 1° are both north, so averaging degrees would be wrong. Each pixel’s aspect is turned into two components, with flat pixels set to 0:
south <- ifel(slope < flat_slope_deg, 0, -cos(aspect * pi / 180))
east  <- ifel(slope < flat_slope_deg, 0,  sin(aspect * pi / 180))
Aspect 180° (south) gives south = 1, east = 0; aspect 90° (east) gives south = 0, east = 1. The parcel value is the coverage-weighted mean of each component.
Extract. One exact_extract(c(elev, slope, south, east), parcels, c("mean", "max", "min")). "mean" weights each pixel by its coverage fraction. "max" and "min" take every pixel the parcel touches, however little, so a parcel smaller than one pixel still gets a range and a maximum slope.

title: Relief
text:
DEM product
The default is Copernicus GLO-30 (1 arc-second, about 30 m; dem_product <- "GLO-30"). Setting dem_product <- "GLO-90" in 00-setup.R and running 00b-download.R switches every step to the 90 m product. GLO-30 covers Poltava oblast plus 10 km with 11 one-degree tiles, and 05-relief.R runs in about 40 seconds.

title: Relief
text:
Limitations

A surface model, not a terrain model
The Copernicus DEM is a digital surface model: it shows the height of the top surface, including buildings and tree canopy, not the bare ground. Water surfaces are flattened. In this dataset, 89 parcels on the Kremenchuk reservoir and other water bodies have a mean slope of 0 and an elevation range of 0, and their aspect variables are 0 (all pixels flat). Over forests and towns, slopes include canopy and building edges.


Coarser tiles north of 50°N
Copernicus tiles have a longitude spacing that grows with latitude: 1 arc-second south of 50°N, but 1.5 arc-seconds from 50°N to 60°N. Poltava oblast spans both zones (its northern strip lies above 50°N).
The virtual mosaic is built in 00b-download.R with vrt(files_ok, options = c("-resolution", "highest")), so the mosaic sits on the finest grid, 1 arc-second. GDAL fills that grid from the coarser northern tiles by repeating their pixels (nearest neighbour, on the fly, when the data are read). No other resampling takes place, and no new elevation values are invented.
The cost: in the northern strip, one column in every three repeats its neighbour. That can add small stair-steps in the east–west direction to slope and aspect there. Comparisons with other implementations in the north of the oblast should allow for this.

title: Relief
text:
Script: 05-relief.R

# 05-relief.R
# In:  data/clean/reference/parcels.parquet, data/interim/dem.vrt
# Out: data/interim/long_relief.parquet
# Purpose: relief per parcel (elevation, slope, aspect exposure) from the whole parcel polygon.
#
# The DEM is cropped only, never resampled or reprojected (EPSG:4326, elevation in metres).
# Slope and aspect come from terra::terrain() on the lon/lat grid. terra's help page (?terra::terrain)
# says: "Distances (needed for slope and aspect) for longitude/latitude data are computed on the
# WGS84 ellipsoid with Karney's algorithm." So no degrees are treated as metres.
# Aspect is clockwise from north, in degrees. A flat pixel (slope < flat_slope_deg) gets 0 for
# both exposure variables: south = -cos(aspect), east = sin(aspect).
# Statistics use exact_extract(): "mean" weights each pixel by the share of it inside the parcel;
# "max" and "min" use every pixel the parcel touches, so a parcel smaller than one pixel still gets values.

source("00-setup.R")

# Parcels and DEM -------------------------------------------------------------

parcels <- arrow::read_parquet(parcels_path, as_data_frame = FALSE) |> st_as_sf()

# Parcels' extent plus 0.02 degrees, so terrain() has neighbours at the edge of every parcel
parcels_box <- ext(vect(parcels)) + 0.02

elev <- crop(rast(dem_vrt_path), parcels_box)
names(elev) <- "elev"

# Slope, aspect and exposure --------------------------------------------------

slope_aspect <- terrain(elev, c("slope", "aspect"), unit = "degrees")
slope <- slope_aspect[["slope"]]
aspect <- slope_aspect[["aspect"]]

south <- ifel(slope < flat_slope_deg, 0, -cos(aspect * pi / 180))
east <- ifel(slope < flat_slope_deg, 0, sin(aspect * pi / 180))

relief <- c(elev, slope, south, east)
names(relief) <- c("elev", "slope", "south", "east")

# Parcel values ---------------------------------------------------------------

relief_stats <- exact_extract(relief, parcels, c("mean", "max", "min"), append_cols = "parcel_id", progress = FALSE)

relief_wide <- relief_stats |>
  transmute(
    parcel_id,
    relief_elev_mean = mean.elev,
    relief_slope_mean = mean.slope,
    relief_slope_max = max.slope,
    relief_elev_range = max.elev - min.elev,
    relief_aspect_south = mean.south,
    relief_aspect_east = mean.east
  )

long_relief <- relief_wide |>
  pivot_longer(-parcel_id, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(source = "observed")

if (anyNA(long_relief$value)) cli_abort("Some relief values are missing.")
if (nrow(long_relief) != 6 * nrow(parcels)) cli_abort("Expected 6 relief rows per parcel, got {nrow(long_relief)} rows.")

# Range of each variable
long_relief |>
  group_by(variable) |>
  summarise(min = min(value), max = max(value)) |>
  print()

# Save ------------------------------------------------------------------------

gc()   # release memory-mapped files before overwriting (Windows)
arrow::write_parquet(long_relief, long_relief_path)

cli_inform("Relief done: {n_distinct(long_relief$variable)} variables, {nrow(long_relief)} rows in {.path {long_relief_path}}.")

title: Pipeline
text:
Design rules

Simple code for novices. tidyverse, sf, terra and exactextractr; short scripts and few comments. No helper functions, no package code, no regular expressions. File paths, year labels and variable names are written out in full, and each crop year has its own block.
No reprojection or resampling of rasters. Each extraction transforms the parcels to the raster’s own CRS instead. The only raster operations are the virtual DEM mosaic, crop(), per-pixel arithmetic on rasters that share a grid, and terrain().
Projections. crs_work <- "EPSG:3035" (equal-area, metres) is used to build the parcel shapes, compute area_ha and draw the maps. Distances are measured on the sphere, in EPSG:4326.
One long table. Columns parcel_id | variable | value | source. Each measurement method is its own variable (_mean, _centroid, _edge, _max, _range).
Guard checks. Scripts stop with cli_abort() when a check fails: row counts, missing values, value ranges.

title: Pipeline
text:
Download script

# 00b-download.R
# In:  internet only
#      - OCHA COD-AB Ukraine admin boundaries, shapefile zip (81.5 MB), licence CC BY-IGO
#        https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-ukr
#        -> data/raw/cod-ab/ukr_admin_boundaries.shp.zip (ADM1 files unzipped next to it)
#      - Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (or GLO-90), tiles over Poltava oblast plus 10 km (about 12 tiles, 20-40 MB each for GLO-30)
#        licence: Copernicus DEM licence (free use, attribution "produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 (c) DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and (c) Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018")
#        https://copernicus-dem-30m.s3.amazonaws.com (GLO-30), https://copernicus-dem-90m.s3.amazonaws.com (GLO-90)
#        -> data/raw/dem/GLO-30/<tile id>.tif
# Out: data/interim/oblasts.gpkg (all oblasts), data/interim/dem.vrt (virtual mosaic of the DEM tiles)
# Purpose: download the public inputs once; existing files are skipped.

source("00-setup.R")

dir.create(codab_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(dem_dir, dem_product), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

h <- curl::new_handle(ssl_options = 2)  # this network cannot check certificate revocation

# COD-AB oblast boundaries (ADM1) ---------------------------------------------

codab_url <- "https://data.humdata.org/dataset/d23f529f-31e4-4021-a65b-13987e5cfb42/resource/2b38131d-5dd6-4b0f-b4c6-4aecc67f179d/download/ukr_admin_boundaries.shp.zip"
codab_zip <- file.path(codab_dir, "ukr_admin_boundaries.shp.zip")
codab_shp <- file.path(codab_dir, "ukr_admin1.shp")

if (!file.exists(codab_zip)) curl::curl_download(codab_url, codab_zip, handle = h)
if (!file.exists(codab_shp)) {
  unzip(
    codab_zip,
    files = c("ukr_admin1.shp", "ukr_admin1.shx", "ukr_admin1.dbf", "ukr_admin1.prj", "ukr_admin1.cpg"),
    exdir = codab_dir
  )
}

oblasts_raw <- st_read(codab_shp, quiet = TRUE)
cli_inform("COD-AB ADM1 fields: {.field {names(oblasts_raw)}}")

oblasts <- oblasts_raw |>
  select(oblast_pcode = adm1_pcode, oblast_ua = adm1_name1, oblast_en = adm1_name) |>
  st_transform(4326)

cli_inform("Renamed {.field adm1_pcode}, {.field adm1_name1}, {.field adm1_name} to {.field oblast_pcode}, {.field oblast_ua}, {.field oblast_en}.")
cli_inform("{nrow(oblasts)} oblasts read (27 expected).")

study_oblast <- oblasts |> filter(oblast_en == study_oblast_en)
if (nrow(study_oblast) != 1) cli_abort("Study oblast {study_oblast_en} not found in COD-AB.")

st_write(oblasts, oblasts_path, delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
cli_inform("Wrote {.path {oblasts_path}}.")

# Copernicus DEM tiles --------------------------------------------------------

dem_products <- tribble(
  ~product, ~bucket,                                         ~code,
  "GLO-30", "https://copernicus-dem-30m.s3.amazonaws.com",  "10",
  "GLO-90", "https://copernicus-dem-90m.s3.amazonaws.com",  "30"
) |> filter(product == dem_product)

# 1 x 1 degree tile boxes over Ukraine, kept where they touch Poltava plus 10 km
study_buffer <- st_buffer(study_oblast, 10000)
tiles <- st_make_grid(cellsize = 1, offset = c(22, 44), n = c(19, 9), crs = 4326)
tiles <- tiles[lengths(st_intersects(tiles, study_buffer)) > 0]

# Lower-left corner of each tile, from its centre
tile_centres <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(tiles))
lon <- round(tile_centres[, "X"] - 0.5)
lat <- round(tile_centres[, "Y"] - 0.5)

dem_tiles <- tibble(
  id = str_c("Copernicus_DSM_COG_", dem_products$code, "_N", lat, "_00_E", sprintf("%03d", lon), "_00_DEM"),
  url = str_c(dem_products$bucket, "/", id, "/", id, ".tif"),
  dest = file.path(dem_dir, dem_product, str_c(id, ".tif"))
)
cli_inform("{nrow(dem_tiles)} {dem_product} tiles intersect {study_oblast_en} plus 10 km.")

# Download only the tiles not on disk yet (multi_download takes handle options, not a handle)
to_get <- dem_tiles |> filter(!file.exists(dest))
cli_inform("{nrow(to_get)} tiles to download.")
res <- curl::multi_download(to_get$url, to_get$dest, progress = FALSE, ssl_options = 2)

# A failed request (e.g. 404 for a sea tile) leaves an error page on disk: remove it
failed <- res |> filter(status_code != 200)
file.remove(failed$destfile[file.exists(failed$destfile)])

# longitude spacing; GDAL repeats their pixels on that grid on the fly (nearest neighbour)
dem <- vrt(files_ok, filename = dem_vrt_path, options = c("-resolution", "highest"), overwrite = TRUE)

title: Pipeline
text:
Combine script
21-combine.R binds the five long tables and stops if any parcel × variable pair appears twice, if any value is missing, if source has a value outside the four levels, or if a parcel does not have exactly 81 variables.

# 21-combine.R
# In:  data/interim/long_distance.parquet, long_soil.parquet, long_relief.parquet, long_crop.parquet, long_crop_2025.parquet
# Out: output/tables/spatial_covariates.parquet, output/tables/spatial_covariates.csv
# Purpose: bind the five long tables into one table of 81 covariates per parcel and check it.

source("00-setup.R")

long_distance <- arrow::read_parquet(long_distance_path)
long_soil <- arrow::read_parquet(long_soil_path)
long_relief <- arrow::read_parquet(long_relief_path)
long_crop <- arrow::read_parquet(long_crop_path)
long_crop_2025 <- arrow::read_parquet(long_crop_2025_path)

covariates <- bind_rows(long_distance, long_soil, long_relief, long_crop, long_crop_2025) |>
  select(parcel_id, variable, value, source) |>
  arrange(parcel_id, variable)

# Checks ----------------------------------------------------------------------

n_duplicates <- covariates |> count(parcel_id, variable) |> filter(n > 1) |> nrow()
if (n_duplicates > 0) cli_abort("{n_duplicates} parcel x variable combinations appear more than once.")

if (anyNA(covariates)) cli_abort("The combined table has missing values.")

if (!all(covariates$source %in% c("observed", "h3_6", "h3_5", "oblast"))) cli_abort("{.field source} has values outside observed, h3_6, h3_5, oblast.")

variables_per_parcel <- covariates |> count(parcel_id)
if (any(variables_per_parcel$n != 81)) cli_abort("Not every parcel has 81 variables.")
if (n_distinct(covariates$variable) != 81) cli_abort("The table does not have 81 distinct variables.")

# Summary ---------------------------------------------------------------------

cli_inform("Parcels: {n_distinct(covariates$parcel_id)}")
cli_inform("Variables: {n_distinct(covariates$variable)}")
cli_inform("Rows: {nrow(covariates)}")
print(count(covariates, source))

# Write -----------------------------------------------------------------------

gc()
arrow::write_parquet(covariates, covariates_parquet_path)
write_csv(covariates, covariates_csv_path)

cli_inform("Wrote {nrow(covariates)} rows to {.path {covariates_parquet_path}} and {.path {covariates_csv_path}}.")

title: Pipeline
text:
Descriptives script
22-descriptives.R writes the summary tables shown on the indicator pages and on Output.

# 22-descriptives.R
# In:  output/tables/spatial_covariates.parquet, data/clean/reference/parcels.parquet
# Out: output/tables/soil_centroid_vs_polygon.csv, crop_by_year.csv, distance_summary.csv, relief_summary.csv,
#      soil_source_by_case.csv; output/figures/soil_centroid_vs_polygon.png
# Purpose: descriptive statistics of the covariates, printed and saved.

source("00-setup.R")

covariates <- arrow::read_parquet(covariates_parquet_path)
parcels <- arrow::read_parquet(parcels_path, col_select = c(parcel_id, case))   # attributes only, no geometry

# Soil: centroid value vs polygon mean -----------------------------------------

# Units are SoilGrids mapped units (see 04-soil.R)
soil_pairs <- tribble(
  ~property,  ~mean_var,                       ~centroid_var,                       ~label,
  "bdod",     "soil_bdod_0_30cm_mean",         "soil_bdod_0_30cm_centroid",         "bdod (cg/cm³)",
  "cec",      "soil_cec_0_30cm_mean",          "soil_cec_0_30cm_centroid",          "cec (mmol(c)/kg)",
  "cfvo",     "soil_cfvo_0_30cm_mean",         "soil_cfvo_0_30cm_centroid",         "cfvo (cm³/dm³)",
  "clay",     "soil_clay_0_30cm_mean",         "soil_clay_0_30cm_centroid",         "clay (g/kg)",
  "nitrogen", "soil_nitrogen_0_30cm_mean",     "soil_nitrogen_0_30cm_centroid",     "nitrogen (cg/kg)",
  "ocd",      "soil_ocd_0_30cm_mean",          "soil_ocd_0_30cm_centroid",          "ocd (hg/m³)",
  "ocs",      "soil_ocs_0_30cm_mean",          "soil_ocs_0_30cm_centroid",          "ocs (t/ha)",
  "phh2o",    "soil_phh2o_0_30cm_mean",        "soil_phh2o_0_30cm_centroid",        "phh2o (pH × 10)",
  "sand",     "soil_sand_0_30cm_mean",         "soil_sand_0_30cm_centroid",         "sand (g/kg)",
  "silt",     "soil_silt_0_30cm_mean",         "soil_silt_0_30cm_centroid",         "silt (g/kg)"
)

soil_mean <- covariates |>
  inner_join(soil_pairs, by = c("variable" = "mean_var")) |>
  select(parcel_id, property, label, mean_value = value, mean_source = source)

soil_centroid <- covariates |>
  inner_join(soil_pairs, by = c("variable" = "centroid_var")) |>
  select(parcel_id, property, centroid_value = value, centroid_source = source)

soil_compare <- soil_mean |>
  inner_join(soil_centroid, by = c("parcel_id", "property")) |>
  mutate(observed = mean_source == "observed" & centroid_source == "observed")

if (nrow(soil_compare) != 10 * n_distinct(covariates$parcel_id)) cli_abort("Soil pairs do not cover 10 properties for every parcel.")

soil_stats_observed <- soil_compare |>
  filter(observed) |>
  group_by(property, label) |>
  summarise(
    rows = "observed",
    pearson = cor(mean_value, centroid_value),
    spearman = cor(mean_value, centroid_value, method = "spearman"),
    mean_abs_diff = mean(abs(centroid_value - mean_value)),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

soil_stats_all <- soil_compare |>
  group_by(property, label) |>
  summarise(
    rows = "all",
    pearson = cor(mean_value, centroid_value),
    spearman = cor(mean_value, centroid_value, method = "spearman"),
    mean_abs_diff = mean(abs(centroid_value - mean_value)),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

soil_stats <- bind_rows(soil_stats_observed, soil_stats_all) |>
  arrange(property, desc(rows))

if (anyNA(soil_stats$pearson) || anyNA(soil_stats$spearman)) cli_abort("Some soil correlations are missing.")
if (any(abs(soil_stats$pearson) > 1) || any(abs(soil_stats$spearman) > 1)) cli_abort("Soil correlations outside [-1, 1].")

print(soil_stats, n = Inf)
write_csv(soil_stats, soil_centroid_vs_polygon_path)

# Scatter plot, one facet per property. geom_blank() with x and y swapped gives
# each facet the same range on both axes, so the 45° line is a true diagonal.
soil_plot_data <- soil_compare |>
  mutate(fill = if_else(observed, "Observed", "Filled (H3 or oblast mean)"))

soil_plot <- ggplot(soil_plot_data, aes(x = mean_value, y = centroid_value)) +
  geom_blank(aes(x = centroid_value, y = mean_value)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "#52514e", linewidth = 0.4, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = fill), size = 0.9, alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(vars(label), ncol = 5, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("Observed" = "#2a78d6", "Filled (H3 or oblast mean)" = "#eb6834"),
    breaks = c("Observed", "Filled (H3 or oblast mean)")
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2.5, alpha = 1))) +
  labs(
    title = "Soil 0–30 cm: value at the parcel centroid vs mean over the parcel polygon",
    subtitle = "One point per parcel; dashed line: centroid = polygon mean. SoilGrids mapped units.",
    x = "Polygon mean",
    y = "Centroid value",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)
  )

ggsave(soil_centroid_vs_polygon_png_path, soil_plot, width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 200, bg = "white")

# Crop share by group and year ---------------------------------------------------

# Variable names look like crop_ag_2019: split them at "_" into group and year
crop_by_year <- covariates |>
  filter(startsWith(variable, "crop_")) |>
  separate_wider_delim(variable, delim = "_", names = c(NA, "group", "year")) |>
  group_by(year, group) |>
  summarise(
    mean_share = mean(value),
    median_share = median(value),
    share_parcels_above_half = mean(value > 0.5),   # for ag: share of parcels with crop_ag > 0.5
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(year, group)

print(crop_by_year, n = Inf)
cli_inform("Share of parcels with {.field crop_ag} > 0.5, by year:")
print(filter(crop_by_year, group == "ag") |> select(year, share_parcels_above_half))
write_csv(crop_by_year, crop_by_year_path)

# Distance quantiles (metres) ----------------------------------------------------

distance_vars <- c(
  "dist_elevator_centroid", "dist_elevator_edge",
  "dist_road_main_centroid", "dist_road_main_edge",
  "dist_road_local_centroid", "dist_road_local_edge"
)

distance_summary <- covariates |>
  filter(variable %in% distance_vars) |>
  group_by(variable) |>
  summarise(
    unit = "m",
    n = n(),
    min = min(value),
    p05 = quantile(value, 0.05),
    p25 = quantile(value, 0.25),
    median = median(value),
    mean = mean(value),
    p75 = quantile(value, 0.75),
    p95 = quantile(value, 0.95),
    max = max(value)
  )

print(distance_summary, width = Inf)
write_csv(distance_summary, distance_summary_path)

# Relief quantiles -----------------------------------------------------------------

relief_units <- tribble(
  ~variable,             ~unit,
  "relief_elev_mean",    "m",
  "relief_elev_range",   "m",
  "relief_slope_mean",   "degrees",
  "relief_slope_max",    "degrees",
  "relief_aspect_south", "index -1 to 1",
  "relief_aspect_east",  "index -1 to 1"
)

relief_summary <- covariates |>
  inner_join(relief_units, by = "variable") |>
  group_by(variable, unit) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    min = min(value),
    p05 = quantile(value, 0.05),
    p25 = quantile(value, 0.25),
    median = median(value),
    mean = mean(value),
    p75 = quantile(value, 0.75),
    p95 = quantile(value, 0.95),
    max = max(value),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(relief_summary, width = Inf)
write_csv(relief_summary, relief_summary_path)

# Soil source by parcel case ---------------------------------------------------------

# Counts soil rows (parcel x soil variable), 20 per parcel
soil_source_by_case <- covariates |>
  filter(variable %in% c(soil_pairs$mean_var, soil_pairs$centroid_var)) |>
  inner_join(parcels, by = "parcel_id") |>
  mutate(source = factor(source, levels = c("observed", "h3_6", "h3_5", "oblast"))) |>
  count(case, source, .drop = FALSE) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = n) |>
  mutate(total = observed + h3_6 + h3_5 + oblast)

print(soil_source_by_case)
write_csv(soil_source_by_case, soil_source_by_case_path)

cli_inform("Descriptives written to {.path {tables_dir}} and {.path {soil_centroid_vs_polygon_png_path}}.")

title: Spatial covariates for mass valuation of agricultural land
Spatial covariates for mass valuation of agricultural land
text:
What the dataset is for

A gold standard. The parcels, elevators and roads are simulated once and committed to the repository. They never change, so results from different tools can be compared row by row.
Hard cases on purpose. 15 % of the parcels cross an oblast boundary and 15 % sit on soil NoData (towns, rivers, the reservoir), to test how each implementation handles edges and missing data.
Explicit methods. Every choice (distance on the sphere, coverage-weighted polygon means, fill order for missing soil values, the 2025 crop rule) is documented on these pages, next to the code that implements it.

The output is one long table, parcel_id | variable | value | source, with 81,000 rows (see Output).

title: Data
text:
Downloaded by 00b-download.R
The download script skips files already on disk, so a second run downloads nothing. All requests use one curl handle with ssl_options = 2, which turns off the certificate revocation check: on the network where this was built, HTTPS requests to HDX and to the AWS buckets fail with the Schannel error CRYPT_E_NO_REVOCATION_CHECK. Base R download.file() fails there too, so the curl package is used.

Oblast boundaries: OCHA COD-AB Ukraine

Source: OCHA Common Operational Dataset, Administrative Boundaries (COD-AB), Ukraine, via the Humanitarian Data Exchange: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-ukr. File ukr_admin_boundaries.shp.zip (81.5 MB), version of 2026-01-26.
Licence: CC BY-IGO. Attribution: OCHA, COD-AB Ukraine.
Use: the ADM1 layer (27 units). The fields adm1_pcode, adm1_name1 and adm1_name are renamed to oblast_pcode, oblast_ua and oblast_en, and written to data/interim/oblasts.gpkg in EPSG:4326.
Note: COD-AB uses the adjectival English names, so Poltava oblast is "Poltavska" (UA53). In 00-setup.R: study_oblast_en <- "Poltavska".



Elevation: Copernicus DEM GLO-30

Source: Copernicus DEM, GLO-30 (1 arc-second, about 30 m) by default, from the public AWS bucket https://copernicus-dem-30m.s3.amazonaws.com. dem_product <- "GLO-90" in 00-setup.R switches to the 90 m product.
Tiles: the 1° × 1° tiles that intersect Poltava oblast plus a 10 km buffer.
Licence and attribution: © DLR e.V. 2010–2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014–2018, provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved. Free of charge for any use.
Use: the tiles are joined in a virtual mosaic, data/interim/dem.vrt. The Relief page explains how the mosaic handles the tiles north of 50°N.



Optional: OpenStreetMap roads
00b-download.R ends with a commented-out block that reads real OSM roads with osmextract (main = motorway, trunk, primary; local = secondary, tertiary). The reference dataset uses the simulated roads below.

Simulated reference inputs (committed)
01-simulate-reference.R generated the reference inputs once, with set.seed(20261110). They are committed as GeoParquet in EPSG:4326 and are never regenerated: the script aborts if parcels.parquet exists.

How they were built is on the Reference inputs page.

Reading GeoParquet
The sf build used here has no GDAL Parquet driver, so the files are written and read with arrow and geoarrow (loaded in 00-setup.R):
arrow::write_parquet(x, path)                                        # write an sf object
x <- arrow::read_parquet(path, as_data_frame = FALSE) |> st_as_sf()  # read it back as sf
as_data_frame = FALSE is required: without it, the geometry column stays a geoarrow_vctr. The geometry type and CRS are stored as geoarrow metadata on the column; the files have no GeoParquet geo key, so other tools may read the geometry as WKB without a CRS (it is EPSG:4326).

title: Crop cover
Crop cover
text:
The 2025 rule: winter over summer
For 2025 there are two maps: a summer map (all classes) and a winter map that marks only winter cereal (2) and winter rapeseed (3). Winter crops are harvested by midsummer, so the summer map can miss them. 07-crop-2025.R combines the two:

inside each parcel, a pixel takes the winter code where the winter map is 2 or 3, and the summer code otherwise;
winter non-crop classes and winter NoData never overwrite the summer map;
the rule is applied per pixel inside the parcels, never on the whole raster.

Both winter codes belong to ag, so the rule moves area from other groups into ag. In this run it changes the group shares of 135 parcels.
The two maps have the same size but their origins differ by about 2 m (less than a quarter of a pixel). After a guard check (same dimensions, origins less than 5 m apart), the winter map is given the summer map’s extent with ext(winter) <- ext(summer). That matches each winter pixel to its nearest summer pixel, without resampling. exact_extract() then returns both values for every pixel in the parcel, with its coverage fraction, and the shares are computed from the combined code.

title: Distance
text:
Method

Distances on the sphere
Parcels, elevators and roads are kept in EPSG:4326 (longitude/latitude). With sf_use_s2(TRUE), sf measures distances with the s2 library, on a sphere (radius 6,371 km), so no flat projection distorts them. The parcel centroid is also computed on the sphere.


Nearest feature only
For each parcel, st_nearest_feature() finds the nearest feature, and st_distance(..., by_element = TRUE) measures the distance to that feature only. The script wraps this in one line:
nearest_dist <- function(from, to) as.numeric(st_distance(from, to[st_nearest_feature(from, to), ], by_element = TRUE))


Centroid vs edge

Centroid: the distance from the parcel’s centre point.
Edge: the distance from the parcel polygon itself, that is from its closest boundary point. It is 0 when the feature touches or crosses the parcel (some parcels are crossed by a road).

So the edge distance is never larger than the centroid distance. The script checks this for every parcel.


Checks in the script

6 rows per parcel and no missing values.
Edge ≤ centroid for every parcel and feature type.
Spot check: for one parcel of each case, the minimum distance to all features (brute force) matches the nearest-feature distance within 1 mm.
Sphere vs ellipsoid: the same parcel–feature pairs are measured again with sf_use_s2(FALSE), which uses lwgeom on the WGS 84 ellipsoid. The script stops if the mean relative gap reaches 0.5 %.

title: Distance
text:
Script: 03-distance.R

# 03-distance.R
# In:  data/clean/reference/parcels.parquet, elevators.parquet, roads.parquet (EPSG:4326)
# Out: data/interim/long_distance.parquet, output/tables/distance_sphere_vs_ellipsoid.csv
# Purpose: distance in metres from each parcel (centroid and edge) to the nearest elevator, main road and local road.

source("00-setup.R")

parcels <- arrow::read_parquet(parcels_path, as_data_frame = FALSE) |> st_as_sf()
elevators <- arrow::read_parquet(elevators_path, as_data_frame = FALSE) |> st_as_sf()
roads <- arrow::read_parquet(roads_path, as_data_frame = FALSE) |> st_as_sf()

roads_main <- roads |> filter(type == "main")
roads_local <- roads |> filter(type == "local")

# Centroids on the sphere (s2). "Edge" is the parcel polygon itself:
# its distance is 0 when a feature touches or crosses the parcel.
centroids <- st_centroid(st_geometry(parcels))
edges <- st_geometry(parcels)

# Distances on the sphere (s2) --------------------------------------------------

# Distance from each "from" geometry to its nearest feature in "to", in metres
nearest_dist <- function(from, to) as.numeric(st_distance(from, to[st_nearest_feature(from, to), ], by_element = TRUE))

distance_wide <- tibble(
  parcel_id = parcels$parcel_id,
  dist_elevator_centroid = nearest_dist(centroids, elevators),
  dist_elevator_edge = nearest_dist(edges, elevators),
  dist_road_main_centroid = nearest_dist(centroids, roads_main),
  dist_road_main_edge = nearest_dist(edges, roads_main),
  dist_road_local_centroid = nearest_dist(centroids, roads_local),
  dist_road_local_edge = nearest_dist(edges, roads_local)
)

distance_long <- distance_wide |>
  pivot_longer(-parcel_id, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(value = as.numeric(value), source = "observed") |>
  select(parcel_id, variable, value, source)

# Checks ----------------------------------------------------------------------

if (nrow(distance_long) != 6 * nrow(parcels)) cli_abort("Expected 6 rows per parcel.")
if (anyNA(distance_long$value)) cli_abort("Some distances are NA.")
if (any(distance_wide$dist_elevator_edge > distance_wide$dist_elevator_centroid)) cli_abort("Elevator: edge distance above centroid distance.")
if (any(distance_wide$dist_road_main_edge > distance_wide$dist_road_main_centroid)) cli_abort("Main road: edge distance above centroid distance.")
if (any(distance_wide$dist_road_local_edge > distance_wide$dist_road_local_centroid)) cli_abort("Local road: edge distance above centroid distance.")

# Spot check: 3 parcels (one per case) against ALL features, minimum by brute force
spot <- c(which(parcels$case == "interior")[1], which(parcels$case == "border")[1], which(parcels$case == "nodata")[1])

spot_check <- tibble(
  parcel_id = parcels$parcel_id[spot],
  dist_elevator_centroid = apply(st_distance(centroids[spot], elevators), 1, min),
  dist_elevator_edge = apply(st_distance(edges[spot], elevators), 1, min),
  dist_road_main_centroid = apply(st_distance(centroids[spot], roads_main), 1, min),
  dist_road_main_edge = apply(st_distance(edges[spot], roads_main), 1, min),
  dist_road_local_centroid = apply(st_distance(centroids[spot], roads_local), 1, min),
  dist_road_local_edge = apply(st_distance(edges[spot], roads_local), 1, min)
)

spot_gap <- abs(as.matrix(spot_check[, -1]) - as.matrix(distance_wide[spot, -1]))
if (max(spot_gap) > 0.001) cli_abort("Spot check failed: brute-force minimum differs by {round(max(spot_gap), 3)} m.")
cli_inform("Spot check passed for parcels {spot_check$parcel_id} (max gap {signif(max(spot_gap), 3)} m).")

# Sphere vs ellipsoid -----------------------------------------------------------

# The same pairs (same nearest feature), measured on the WGS84 ellipsoid (lwgeom)
idx_elevator_centroid <- st_nearest_feature(centroids, elevators)
idx_elevator_edge <- st_nearest_feature(edges, elevators)
idx_road_main_centroid <- st_nearest_feature(centroids, roads_main)
idx_road_main_edge <- st_nearest_feature(edges, roads_main)
idx_road_local_centroid <- st_nearest_feature(centroids, roads_local)
idx_road_local_edge <- st_nearest_feature(edges, roads_local)

sf_use_s2(FALSE)

ellipsoid_wide <- tibble(
  parcel_id = parcels$parcel_id,
  dist_elevator_centroid = as.numeric(st_distance(centroids, elevators[idx_elevator_centroid, ], by_element = TRUE)),
  dist_elevator_edge = as.numeric(st_distance(edges, elevators[idx_elevator_edge, ], by_element = TRUE)),
  dist_road_main_centroid = as.numeric(st_distance(centroids, roads_main[idx_road_main_centroid, ], by_element = TRUE)),
  dist_road_main_edge = as.numeric(st_distance(edges, roads_main[idx_road_main_edge, ], by_element = TRUE)),
  dist_road_local_centroid = as.numeric(st_distance(centroids, roads_local[idx_road_local_centroid, ], by_element = TRUE)),
  dist_road_local_edge = as.numeric(st_distance(edges, roads_local[idx_road_local_edge, ], by_element = TRUE))
)

sf_use_s2(TRUE)

ellipsoid_long <- ellipsoid_wide |>
  pivot_longer(-parcel_id, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value_ellipsoid")

# Relative gap only where the ellipsoidal distance is above 0 (edge distances can be 0)
distance_check <- distance_long |>
  left_join(ellipsoid_long, by = c("parcel_id", "variable")) |>
  mutate(gap_m = abs(value - value_ellipsoid),
         gap_pct = if_else(value_ellipsoid > 0, 100 * gap_m / value_ellipsoid, NA)) |>
  summarise(mean_gap_m = mean(gap_m),
            max_gap_m = max(gap_m),
            mean_gap_pct = mean(gap_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
            .by = variable)

print(distance_check)
if (any(distance_check$mean_gap_pct >= 0.5)) cli_abort("Mean relative sphere vs ellipsoid gap is 0.5 % or more.")

# Write -----------------------------------------------------------------------

gc()
arrow::write_parquet(distance_long, long_distance_path)
write_csv(distance_check, distance_check_path)

cli_inform("Wrote {nrow(distance_long)} rows to {.path {long_distance_path}} and the check table to {.path {distance_check_path}}.")

title: Reference inputs
text:
The parcels, elevators and roads are simulated. 01-simulate-reference.R generated them once with set.seed(20261110), and they are committed to the repository as GeoParquet in EPSG:4326 (data/clean/reference/). They are a fixed gold standard: the script aborts if the files already exist, so they are never regenerated by accident.
All shapes are built in EPSG:3035 (equal-area, metres) inside Poltava oblast (oblast_en == "Poltavska" in COD-AB). Its neighbours are the oblasts that touch it: Chernihivska, Sumska, Kharkivska, Dnipropetrovska, Kirovohradska, Cherkaska and Kyivska.

title: Reference inputs
text:
Parcels

Three cases









Case
Parcels
How the centre is drawn
What it tests




interior
700
Random point in Poltava, more than 1 km from its boundary
The normal case


border
150
Random point on the part of Poltava’s boundary shared with a neighbouring oblast
Parcels that cross an oblast boundary


nodata
150
Random soil NoData cell (SoilGrids clay 0–5 cm) inside Poltava shrunk by 1 km, shifted by at most 100 m
Missing soil data: towns, rivers, the Kremenchuk reservoir



The script checks that:

every border parcel intersects Poltava and at least one neighbour;
at least 70 % of the nodata parcels have more than half of their area on soil NoData;
among the nodata parcels, at least 30 are mostly built-up (crop code 1 is the majority pixel in 2024) and at least 30 have water (codes 13 or 14) inside the parcel or within 500 m.



Shapes
Each parcel is a rectangle or a parallelogram, built from a unit square by scale → shear → rotate → translate:

area: pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n, log(3), 0.25), 1), 10) hectares, so all parcels are 1–10 ha and most (at least 75 %, checked) are 2–4 ha;
aspect ratio (length / width): uniform 1.5–6;
rotation angle: uniform 0–π;
shear: 0 for half of the parcels (rectangles), uniform 0.2–0.5 for the others (parallelograms). The shear keeps the area.



Attributes







Column
Meaning




parcel_id
P00001 … P01000 (P00001–P00700 interior, P00701–P00850 border, P00851–P01000 nodata)


case
interior, border or nodata


area_ha
Area in hectares, from st_area() in EPSG:3035


oblast
COD-AB English name of the oblast with the largest overlap


h3_6, h3_5
H3 cell IDs (resolution 6, about 34 km²; resolution 5, about 240 km² in Poltava) of the parcel centroid in WGS 84, from h3o::h3_from_points(). Used to fill missing soil values

title: Reference inputs
text:
Elevators
30 random points inside Poltava (st_sample()), with elevator_id E001 … E030.

title: Reference inputs
text:
Roads

Main roads (4). 40 candidate straight lines are drawn between pairs of random points on Poltava’s boundary and clipped to Poltava. The 4 longest are kept (M01–M04), so each main road crosses the oblast from boundary to boundary (all are longer than 50 km, checked).
Local roads (50). Lines of 5–20 km from random points inside Poltava in a random direction, clipped to Poltava (L01–L50).
Densified. All roads are segmentized with st_segmentize(dfMaxLength = 950) in EPSG:3035, so that segments stay under 1 km when measured on the sphere too (the projection distorts lengths slightly). Distances on the sphere follow great circles between vertices, so short segments keep the spherical line close to the straight line drawn in the projection.

title: Reference inputs
text:
Scripts

01-simulate-reference.R

# 01-simulate-reference.R
# In:  data/interim/oblasts.gpkg, clay_0-5cm_mean.tif (soil NoData cells), crop_2024 (only to check towns and water)
# Out: data/clean/reference/parcels.parquet, elevators.parquet, roads.parquet (GeoParquet, EPSG:4326)
# Purpose: simulate the fixed reference parcels, elevators and roads in Poltava oblast.
# This script ran once to create the committed reference inputs. It is not part of the normal run.

source("00-setup.R")

if (file.exists(parcels_path)) cli_abort("Reference inputs already exist. They are fixed: do not regenerate.")

set.seed(20261110)

# Study oblast and its neighbours, in metres ----------------------------------

oblasts <- st_read(oblasts_path, quiet = TRUE) |> st_transform(crs_work)
poltava <- oblasts |> filter(oblast_en == study_oblast_en)
neighbours <- oblasts |> filter(lengths(st_touches(oblasts, poltava)) > 0)
poltava_inner <- st_buffer(poltava, -1000)   # Poltava shrunk by 1 km

cli_inform("{study_oblast_en} has {nrow(neighbours)} neighbouring oblasts.")

# Parcel centres --------------------------------------------------------------

# interior: random points more than 1 km from Poltava's boundary
interior <- st_sample(poltava, 900) |>
  st_as_sf() |>
  st_filter(poltava_inner) |>
  slice_head(n = 700) |>
  mutate(case = "interior")

# border: random points on the boundary Poltava shares with its neighbours
shared_boundary <- st_intersection(st_boundary(st_geometry(poltava)), st_union(neighbours)) |>
  st_line_merge()   # one line, so that st_sample() spreads the points along its whole length
border <- st_sample(shared_boundary, 150, type = "random", exact = TRUE) |>
  st_as_sf() |>
  st_cast("POINT") |>
  slice_head(n = 150) |>
  mutate(case = "border")

# nodata: random soil NoData cells (towns, rivers, reservoir) inside Poltava shrunk by 1 km
clay <- rast(file.path(soil_dir, "clay_0-5cm_mean.tif"))
clay_crop <- crop(clay, st_transform(poltava_inner, crs(clay)))
soil_na_cells <- ifel(is.na(clay_crop), 1, NA)   # 1 on soil NoData, NA elsewhere

nodata_cells <- spatSample(soil_na_cells, size = 5000, method = "random", na.rm = TRUE, as.points = TRUE) |>
  st_as_sf() |>
  st_transform(crs_work) |>
  st_filter(poltava_inner) |>
  slice_sample(n = 150)

# shift each nodata centre by at most 100 m in a random direction
shift_m <- runif(150, 0, 100)
shift_angle <- runif(150, 0, 2 * pi)
nodata_xy <- st_coordinates(nodata_cells)
nodata <- tibble(
  case = "nodata",
  x = nodata_xy[, "X"] + shift_m * cos(shift_angle),
  y = nodata_xy[, "Y"] + shift_m * sin(shift_angle)
) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = crs_work)

centres <- bind_rows(
  interior |> st_set_geometry("geometry"),
  border |> st_set_geometry("geometry"),
  nodata
)
centres_xy <- st_coordinates(centres)

# Parcel shapes: unit square -> scale -> shear -> rotate -> translate ---------

shapes <- tibble(
  case = centres$case,
  x = centres_xy[, "X"],
  y = centres_xy[, "Y"]
) |>
  mutate(
    area_target = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n(), log(3), 0.25), 1), 10),   # hectares
    ratio = runif(n(), 1.5, 6),
    angle = runif(n(), 0, pi),
    shear = if_else(runif(n()) < 0.5, 0, runif(n(), 0.2, 0.5))
  )

shapes$geometry <- pmap(
  list(shapes$x, shapes$y, shapes$area_target, shapes$ratio, shapes$angle, shapes$shear),
  \(x, y, area_target, ratio, angle, shear) {
    square <- matrix(c(-0.5, -0.5, 0.5, -0.5, 0.5, 0.5, -0.5, 0.5, -0.5, -0.5), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)
    width <- sqrt(area_target * 10000 / ratio)
    scaled <- square %*% diag(c(width * ratio, width))
    sheared <- scaled %*% matrix(c(1, 0, shear, 1), ncol = 2)   # y + shear * x keeps the area
    rotated <- sheared %*% matrix(c(cos(angle), -sin(angle), sin(angle), cos(angle)), ncol = 2)
    st_polygon(list(sweep(rotated, 2, c(x, y), "+")))
  }
) |>
  st_sfc(crs = crs_work)

parcels <- shapes |>
  st_as_sf() |>
  mutate(
    parcel_id = sprintf("P%05d", row_number()),
    area_ha = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 10000
  ) |>
  select(parcel_id, case, area_ha)

# Oblast with the largest overlap
parcel_oblast <- st_intersection(parcels, select(oblasts, oblast_en)) |>
  mutate(overlap = as.numeric(st_area(geometry))) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(parcel_id) |>
  slice_max(overlap, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(parcel_id, oblast = oblast_en)

parcels <- parcels |> left_join(parcel_oblast, by = "parcel_id")

# H3 cells of the WGS84 centroid
parcels_4326 <- st_transform(parcels, 4326)
centroids_4326 <- st_centroid(st_geometry(parcels_4326))
parcels_4326 <- parcels_4326 |>
  mutate(
    h3_6 = h3o::h3_from_points(centroids_4326, 6) |> as.character(),
    h3_5 = h3o::h3_from_points(centroids_4326, 5) |> as.character()
  ) |>
  select(parcel_id, case, area_ha, oblast, h3_6, h3_5)

# Elevators -------------------------------------------------------------------

elevators <- st_sample(poltava, 30) |>
  st_as_sf() |>
  st_set_geometry("geometry") |>
  mutate(elevator_id = sprintf("E%03d", row_number())) |>
  select(elevator_id)

# Roads -----------------------------------------------------------------------

# main: 40 candidate straight lines between random points on Poltava's boundary.
# After clipping to Poltava, the 4 longest are kept, so every main road crosses Poltava.
main_ends <- st_sample(st_line_merge(st_boundary(st_geometry(poltava))), 80, type = "random", exact = TRUE) |>
  st_cast("POINT") |>
  st_coordinates()
main_roads <- tibble(
  road_id = rep(sprintf("C%02d", 1:40), each = 2),
  type = "main",
  x = main_ends[1:80, "X"],
  y = main_ends[1:80, "Y"]
) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = crs_work) |>
  group_by(road_id, type) |>
  summarise(do_union = FALSE, .groups = "drop") |>
  st_cast("LINESTRING") |>
  st_intersection(st_geometry(poltava)) |>   # a road that leaves Poltava and comes back becomes a MULTILINESTRING
  st_collection_extract("LINESTRING") |>     # drop stray points from the clipping
  mutate(length_m = as.numeric(st_length(geometry))) |>
  slice_max(length_m, n = 4, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(road_id = sprintf("M%02d", row_number()))

# local: 50 lines of 5-20 km from random points inside Poltava, in a random direction
local_starts <- st_coordinates(st_sample(poltava, 50))
local_length <- runif(50, 5000, 20000)
local_angle <- runif(50, 0, 2 * pi)
local_roads <- bind_rows(
  tibble(road_id = sprintf("L%02d", 1:50), x = local_starts[, "X"], y = local_starts[, "Y"]),
  tibble(
    road_id = sprintf("L%02d", 1:50),
    x = local_starts[, "X"] + local_length * cos(local_angle),
    y = local_starts[, "Y"] + local_length * sin(local_angle)
  )
) |>
  arrange(road_id) |>
  mutate(type = "local") |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = crs_work) |>
  group_by(road_id, type) |>
  summarise(do_union = FALSE, .groups = "drop") |>
  st_cast("LINESTRING") |>
  st_intersection(st_geometry(poltava))

# densify to 950 m here, so that segments stay under 1 km on the sphere too
roads <- bind_rows(main_roads, local_roads) |>
  st_segmentize(dfMaxLength = 950) |>
  select(road_id, type)

# Summaries -------------------------------------------------------------------

print(count(st_drop_geometry(parcels_4326), case))
print(summary(parcels_4326$area_ha))
print(count(st_drop_geometry(roads), type))

# Checks ----------------------------------------------------------------------

share_2_4_ha <- mean(parcels_4326$area_ha >= 2 & parcels_4326$area_ha <= 4)
cli_inform("{round(100 * share_2_4_ha, 1)}% of parcels are 2-4 ha (75% or more expected).")
if (share_2_4_ha < 0.75) cli_abort("Too few parcels of 2-4 ha.")
if (any(parcels_4326$area_ha < 1 | parcels_4326$area_ha > 10)) cli_abort("Parcel areas must be 1-10 ha.")
if (n_distinct(parcels_4326$parcel_id) != n_parcels) cli_abort("Parcel IDs are not unique.")
if (!all(st_is_valid(parcels_4326))) cli_abort("Some parcel geometries are invalid.")

border_parcels <- parcels |> filter(case == "border")
border_in_poltava <- lengths(st_intersects(border_parcels, poltava)) > 0
border_in_neighbour <- lengths(st_intersects(border_parcels, neighbours)) > 0
cli_inform("{sum(border_in_poltava & border_in_neighbour)} of {nrow(border_parcels)} border parcels cross into a neighbouring oblast.")
if (!all(border_in_poltava & border_in_neighbour)) cli_abort("Every border parcel must touch Poltava and a neighbour.")

# Share of each nodata parcel on soil NoData
nodata_parcels <- parcels |> filter(case == "nodata")
soil_na_share <- exact_extract(is.na(clay_crop), st_transform(nodata_parcels, crs(clay)), "mean", progress = FALSE)
share_mostly_na <- mean(soil_na_share > 0.5)
cli_inform("{round(100 * share_mostly_na, 1)}% of nodata parcels are more than half on soil NoData (70% or more expected).")
if (share_mostly_na < 0.7) cli_abort("Too few nodata parcels on soil NoData.")

# Towns and water around nodata parcels, from the 2024 crop map
crop24 <- rast(crop_2024)
nodata_crop <- st_transform(nodata_parcels, crs(crop24))
crop_majority <- exact_extract(crop24, nodata_crop, "mode", progress = FALSE)
crop_near <- exact_extract(crop24, st_buffer(nodata_crop, 500), "frac", progress = FALSE)
n_town <- sum(crop_majority == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
n_water <- sum(crop_near$frac_13 + crop_near$frac_14 > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
cli_inform("{n_town} nodata parcels are mostly built (code 1) in 2024; {n_water} have water within 500 m (30 or more each expected).")
if (n_town < 30) cli_abort("Fewer than 30 nodata parcels near a town.")
if (n_water < 30) cli_abort("Fewer than 30 nodata parcels near water.")

if (!all(st_within(elevators, poltava, sparse = FALSE))) cli_abort("Some elevators lie outside Poltava.")
if (!all(st_covered_by(roads, st_buffer(poltava, 1), sparse = FALSE))) cli_abort("Some roads lie outside Poltava.")
if (!all(st_geometry_type(roads) %in% c("LINESTRING", "MULTILINESTRING"))) cli_abort("Some roads are not lines.")
if (any(main_roads$length_m < 50000)) cli_abort("Some main roads are shorter than 50 km.")

# Write in EPSG:4326 ----------------------------------------------------------

arrow::write_parquet(parcels_4326, parcels_path)
arrow::write_parquet(st_transform(elevators, 4326), elevators_path)
arrow::write_parquet(st_transform(roads, 4326), roads_path)
cli_inform("Wrote {.path {parcels_path}}, {.path {elevators_path}} and {.path {roads_path}}.")



02-diagnostics.R

# 02-diagnostics.R
# In:  data/interim/oblasts.gpkg, data/clean/reference/*.parquet, clay_0-5cm_mean.tif (soil NoData area)
# Out: output/figures/parcels-map.png, output/figures/parcels-zoom.png
# Purpose: map the reference inputs and print parcel counts and areas by case and oblast.

source("00-setup.R")

# Inputs, in metres ------------------------------------------------------------

oblasts <- st_read(oblasts_path, quiet = TRUE) |> st_transform(crs_work) |> st_set_agr("constant")   # attributes hold for every part of a shape
poltava <- oblasts |> filter(oblast_en == study_oblast_en)
neighbours <- oblasts |> filter(lengths(st_touches(oblasts, poltava)) > 0)

parcels <- arrow::read_parquet(parcels_path, as_data_frame = FALSE) |> st_as_sf() |> st_transform(crs_work) |> st_set_agr("constant")
elevators <- arrow::read_parquet(elevators_path, as_data_frame = FALSE) |> st_as_sf() |> st_transform(crs_work)
roads <- arrow::read_parquet(roads_path, as_data_frame = FALSE) |> st_as_sf() |> st_transform(crs_work)

# Map window: Poltava plus 20 km
map_box <- st_bbox(st_buffer(poltava, 20000))
map_window <- st_as_sfc(map_box)

# Soil NoData area -------------------------------------------------------------

# The raster stays in its own CRS: NoData cells become polygons, and only those vectors are transformed
clay <- rast(file.path(soil_dir, "clay_0-5cm_mean.tif"))
clay_crop <- crop(clay, st_transform(map_window, crs(clay)))
soil_na <- ifel(is.na(clay_crop), 1, NA) |>   # 1 on soil NoData, NA elsewhere
  as.polygons() |>
  st_as_sf() |>
  st_transform(crs_work) |>
  st_make_valid()

# Counts and areas by case and oblast ------------------------------------------

parcel_table <- parcels |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(case, oblast) |>
  summarise(
    n_parcels = n(),
    area_ha_total = round(sum(area_ha), 1),
    area_ha_mean = round(mean(area_ha), 2),
    area_ha_min = round(min(area_ha), 2),
    area_ha_max = round(max(area_ha), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(case, desc(n_parcels))

print(parcel_table, n = Inf)

# Colours ----------------------------------------------------------------------

case_colours <- c(interior = "#2a78d6", border = "#eb6834", nodata = "#1baf7a")
nodata_fill <- "#d3d1c8"
ink <- "#0b0b0b"
ink_secondary <- "#52514e"
ink_muted <- "#898781"

# Overview map -----------------------------------------------------------------

# At this scale a 3 ha parcel is about 2 pixels wide, so parcels are drawn as centroid points
parcel_points <- st_centroid(parcels)
neighbour_labels <- st_intersection(neighbours, map_window) |> st_set_agr("constant") |> st_point_on_surface()

parcels_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = neighbours, fill = "#f4f3ef", colour = ink_muted, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = poltava, fill = "#fcfcfb", colour = ink_secondary, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_sf(data = soil_na, aes(fill = "Soil NoData (towns, water)"), colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = roads, aes(linewidth = type), colour = ink_secondary) +
  geom_sf(data = parcel_points, aes(colour = case), size = 1.1) +
  geom_sf(data = elevators, aes(shape = "Elevator"), fill = ink, colour = "white", size = 2.6, stroke = 0.4) +
  geom_sf_text(data = neighbour_labels, aes(label = oblast_en), colour = ink_muted, size = 3.2, fontface = "italic") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = case_colours, name = "Parcel case") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = nodata_fill, name = NULL) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(main = 0.8, local = 0.3), name = "Road") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = 24, name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3), order = 1)) +
  coord_sf(xlim = map_box[c("xmin", "xmax")], ylim = map_box[c("ymin", "ymax")], expand = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = str_c("Reference inputs in ", study_oblast_en, " oblast"),
    subtitle = str_c(nrow(parcels), " simulated parcels (centroids), ", nrow(elevators), " elevators, ", nrow(roads), " roads"),
    caption = "Grey shading: SoilGrids clay 0-5 cm NoData. Outlines: oblasts (COD-AB). EPSG:3035."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#fcfcfb", colour = NA),
    panel.grid = element_line(colour = "#e1e0d9", linewidth = 0.2),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 8),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(colour = ink, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = ink_secondary),
    plot.caption = element_text(colour = ink_muted, hjust = 0),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

ggsave(parcels_map_path, parcels_map, width = 10, height = 7.5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
cli_inform("Wrote {.path {parcels_map_path}}.")

# Zoom: one parcel of each case ------------------------------------------------

# Layers shared by the three panels
zoom_layers <- list(
  geom_sf(data = soil_na, fill = nodata_fill, colour = NA),
  geom_sf(data = st_boundary(oblasts), colour = ink, linewidth = 0.6, linetype = "dashed"),
  geom_sf(data = roads, aes(linewidth = type), colour = ink_secondary, show.legend = FALSE),
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(main = 1.2, local = 0.6)),
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11),
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#fcfcfb", colour = NA),
    panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "#c3c2b7", linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(colour = ink, face = "bold", size = 11),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = ink_secondary, size = 9)
  )
)

title: Soil
text:
Method

Topsoil 0–30 cm
SoilGrids gives each property for the depth layers 0–5, 5–15 and 15–30 cm. One topsoil value is their thickness-weighted average, computed per pixel:
\[
\text{topsoil}_{0\text{–}30} = \frac{5 \cdot d_{0\text{–}5} + 10 \cdot d_{5\text{–}15} + 15 \cdot d_{15\text{–}30}}{30}
\]
The organic carbon stock ocs is already given for 0–30 cm and is used as is.
Each depth raster is first cropped to the extent of Poltava and its neighbouring oblasts, in the soil CRS (Interrupted Goode Homolosine). The arithmetic runs on that cropped grid. The rasters are never resampled or reprojected; the 10 topsoil layers are saved as data/interim/soil_topsoil_0_30cm.tif. The parcels are transformed to the soil CRS instead.


Polygon mean vs centroid

_mean: exactextractr::exact_extract(soil, parcels, "mean"). Every 250 m pixel that the parcel touches counts, weighted by the share of the pixel inside the parcel. NoData pixels are skipped, so a parcel partly on soil data gets the mean of its covered part, and counts as observed.
_centroid: terra::extract() at the parcel centroid: the value of the one pixel under the centre point.

A 3 ha parcel is much smaller than one 250 m pixel (6.25 ha), so the two often agree. They differ when a parcel straddles pixel edges or lies near NoData.


Filling NoData
A parcel on towns, rivers or the reservoir has no soil value. The fill uses the mean of the soil raster over a larger zone around the parcel, in this order:

h3_6: the mean over the parcel’s H3 resolution-6 cell (about 34 km²);
h3_5: if that cell has no soil data, the mean over its H3 resolution-5 cell (about 240 km²);
oblast: if that is empty too, the mean over the parcel’s own oblast (Poltava or a neighbour).

The zone means also use exact_extract(..., "mean"), so they skip NoData pixels. The H3 cell IDs come from the parcel file; the hexagon polygons are rebuilt from the IDs with h3o::h3_from_strings() and st_as_sfc().
In code:
value = coalesce(value_raw, h3_6_value, h3_5_value, oblast_value)
source = case_when(!is.na(value_raw) ~ "observed", !is.na(h3_6_value) ~ "h3_6",
                   !is.na(h3_5_value) ~ "h3_5", !is.na(oblast_value) ~ "oblast")
The fill is applied to the _mean and _centroid variables separately: a parcel can have an observed polygon mean and a filled centroid value. In this run, 16,100 soil rows are observed, 3,400 are filled from H3 resolution 6, 500 from H3 resolution 5, and none from the oblast mean. Most filled rows belong to the nodata parcels, as intended:

text:
Script: 04-soil.R

# 04-soil.R
# In:  data/clean/reference/parcels.parquet, data/interim/oblasts.gpkg, 28 SoilGrids rasters in soil_dir
# Out: data/interim/soil_topsoil_0_30cm.tif, data/interim/long_soil.parquet
# Purpose: topsoil (0-30 cm) soil properties per parcel (polygon mean and centroid), with NoData filled.
#
# Units are SoilGrids mapped units (not converted):
#   bdod cg/cm3, cec mmol(c)/kg, cfvo cm3/dm3, clay g/kg, nitrogen cg/kg,
#   ocd hg/m3, phh2o pH x 10, sand g/kg, silt g/kg, ocs t/ha (already 0-30 cm).
# Topsoil = (5 * d0_5 + 10 * d5_15 + 15 * d15_30) / 30, per pixel.
# NoData fill order: H3 res-6 cell mean -> H3 res-5 cell mean -> oblast mean.
# The level used goes in `source`. A parcel partly covered by soil data counts as "observed".

source("00-setup.R")

# Parcels and study area in the soil CRS --------------------------------------

parcels <- arrow::read_parquet(parcels_path, as_data_frame = FALSE) |> st_as_sf()
oblasts <- st_read(oblasts_path, quiet = TRUE)

poltava <- oblasts |> filter(oblast_en == study_oblast_en)
study_oblasts <- oblasts |> filter(lengths(st_intersects(oblasts, poltava)) > 0)   # Poltava and its neighbours

soil_crs <- crs(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "clay_0-5cm_mean.tif")))   # Interrupted Goode Homolosine

parcels_soil <- st_transform(parcels, soil_crs)
study_oblasts_soil <- st_transform(study_oblasts, soil_crs)
study_box <- vect(study_oblasts_soil)   # crop() uses its extent

cli_inform("Study area: {study_oblast_en} and {nrow(study_oblasts) - 1} neighbouring oblasts.")

# Topsoil 0-30 cm rasters -----------------------------------------------------

# Topsoil 0-30 cm: thickness-weighted average of the 0-5, 5-15 and 15-30 cm layers
soil_bdod_0_30cm <- (5  * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "bdod_0-5cm_mean.tif")),   study_box) +
                     10 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "bdod_5-15cm_mean.tif")),  study_box) +
                     15 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "bdod_15-30cm_mean.tif")), study_box)) / 30

soil_cec_0_30cm <- (5  * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "cec_0-5cm_mean.tif")),   study_box) +
                    10 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "cec_5-15cm_mean.tif")),  study_box) +
                    15 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "cec_15-30cm_mean.tif")), study_box)) / 30

soil_cfvo_0_30cm <- (5  * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "cfvo_0-5cm_mean.tif")),   study_box) +
                     10 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "cfvo_5-15cm_mean.tif")),  study_box) +
                     15 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "cfvo_15-30cm_mean.tif")), study_box)) / 30

soil_clay_0_30cm <- (5  * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "clay_0-5cm_mean.tif")),   study_box) +
                     10 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "clay_5-15cm_mean.tif")),  study_box) +
                     15 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "clay_15-30cm_mean.tif")), study_box)) / 30

soil_nitrogen_0_30cm <- (5  * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "nitrogen_0-5cm_mean.tif")),   study_box) +
                         10 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "nitrogen_5-15cm_mean.tif")),  study_box) +
                         15 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "nitrogen_15-30cm_mean.tif")), study_box)) / 30

soil_ocd_0_30cm <- (5  * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "ocd_0-5cm_mean.tif")),   study_box) +
                    10 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "ocd_5-15cm_mean.tif")),  study_box) +
                    15 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "ocd_15-30cm_mean.tif")), study_box)) / 30

soil_phh2o_0_30cm <- (5  * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "phh2o_0-5cm_mean.tif")),   study_box) +
                      10 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "phh2o_5-15cm_mean.tif")),  study_box) +
                      15 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "phh2o_15-30cm_mean.tif")), study_box)) / 30

soil_sand_0_30cm <- (5  * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "sand_0-5cm_mean.tif")),   study_box) +
                     10 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "sand_5-15cm_mean.tif")),  study_box) +
                     15 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "sand_15-30cm_mean.tif")), study_box)) / 30

soil_silt_0_30cm <- (5  * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "silt_0-5cm_mean.tif")),   study_box) +
                     10 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "silt_5-15cm_mean.tif")),  study_box) +
                     15 * crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "silt_15-30cm_mean.tif")), study_box)) / 30

# Organic carbon stock is already given for 0-30 cm
soil_ocs_0_30cm <- crop(rast(file.path(soil_dir, "ocs_0-30cm_mean.tif")), study_box)

soil <- c(soil_bdod_0_30cm, soil_cec_0_30cm, soil_cfvo_0_30cm, soil_clay_0_30cm, soil_nitrogen_0_30cm,
          soil_ocd_0_30cm, soil_phh2o_0_30cm, soil_sand_0_30cm, soil_silt_0_30cm, soil_ocs_0_30cm)
names(soil) <- c("soil_bdod_0_30cm", "soil_cec_0_30cm", "soil_cfvo_0_30cm", "soil_clay_0_30cm",
                 "soil_nitrogen_0_30cm", "soil_ocd_0_30cm", "soil_phh2o_0_30cm", "soil_sand_0_30cm",
                 "soil_silt_0_30cm", "soil_ocs_0_30cm")

writeRaster(soil, soil_topsoil_path, overwrite = TRUE)
soil <- rast(soil_topsoil_path)

# Parcel values ---------------------------------------------------------------

# Polygon mean, weighted by the share of each pixel inside the parcel (NoData pixels are skipped)
soil_mean <- exact_extract(soil, parcels_soil, "mean", append_cols = "parcel_id", progress = FALSE) |>
  pivot_longer(-parcel_id, names_to = "property", names_prefix = "mean.", values_to = "value_raw") |>
  mutate(variable = paste0(property, "_mean"))

# Value of the pixel under the parcel centroid
soil_centroid <- terra::extract(soil, vect(st_centroid(parcels_soil)), ID = FALSE) |>
  mutate(parcel_id = parcels_soil$parcel_id) |>
  pivot_longer(-parcel_id, names_to = "property", values_to = "value_raw") |>
  mutate(variable = paste0(property, "_centroid"))

soil_long <- bind_rows(soil_mean, soil_centroid) |>
  mutate(value_raw = if_else(is.nan(value_raw), NA, value_raw)) |>   # a parcel with no soil data gives NaN
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(parcels) |> select(parcel_id, case, oblast, h3_6, h3_5), by = "parcel_id")

# =============================================================================
# FILL ZONES
# Mean soil value in each zone, used where a parcel has no soil data.
# To use rayon or hromada polygons instead of H3 cells, read COD-AB ADM2 (rayon)
# or ADM3 (hromada) from data/raw/cod-ab, add the zone code to the parcels with
# st_join(), and replace the H3 zones below with those polygons and codes.
# =============================================================================

# H3 hexagons of the parcels' cells, built from the cell IDs
hex_6 <- tibble(h3_6 = unique(parcels$h3_6)) |>
  mutate(geometry = h3o::h3_from_strings(h3_6) |> st_as_sfc()) |>
  st_as_sf() |>
  st_transform(soil_crs)

hex_5 <- tibble(h3_5 = unique(parcels$h3_5)) |>
  mutate(geometry = h3o::h3_from_strings(h3_5) |> st_as_sfc()) |>
  st_as_sf() |>
  st_transform(soil_crs)

zone_h3_6 <- exact_extract(soil, hex_6, "mean", append_cols = "h3_6", progress = FALSE) |>
  pivot_longer(-h3_6, names_to = "property", names_prefix = "mean.", values_to = "h3_6_value")

zone_h3_5 <- exact_extract(soil, hex_5, "mean", append_cols = "h3_5", progress = FALSE) |>
  pivot_longer(-h3_5, names_to = "property", names_prefix = "mean.", values_to = "h3_5_value")

# Oblast mean, for Poltava and its neighbours (joined on the parcel's oblast)
zone_oblast <- exact_extract(soil, study_oblasts_soil, "mean", append_cols = "oblast_en", progress = FALSE) |>
  rename(oblast = oblast_en) |>
  pivot_longer(-oblast, names_to = "property", names_prefix = "mean.", values_to = "oblast_value")

# Fill ------------------------------------------------------------------------

soil_long <- soil_long |>
  left_join(zone_h3_6, by = c("h3_6", "property")) |>
  left_join(zone_h3_5, by = c("h3_5", "property")) |>
  left_join(zone_oblast, by = c("oblast", "property")) |>
  mutate(
    h3_6_value = if_else(is.nan(h3_6_value), NA, h3_6_value),
    h3_5_value = if_else(is.nan(h3_5_value), NA, h3_5_value),
    value = coalesce(value_raw, h3_6_value, h3_5_value, oblast_value),
    source = case_when(
      !is.na(value_raw) ~ "observed",
      !is.na(h3_6_value) ~ "h3_6",
      !is.na(h3_5_value) ~ "h3_5",
      !is.na(oblast_value) ~ "oblast"
    )
  )

if (anyNA(soil_long$value)) cli_abort("Some soil values are still missing after the fill.")
if (nrow(soil_long) != 20 * nrow(parcels)) cli_abort("Expected 20 soil rows per parcel, got {nrow(soil_long)} rows.")

# Counts by source and case
soil_long |> count(source, case) |> print()

# Save ------------------------------------------------------------------------

long_soil <- soil_long |> select(parcel_id, variable, value, source)

gc()   # release memory-mapped files before overwriting (Windows)
arrow::write_parquet(long_soil, long_soil_path)

cli_inform("Soil done: {n_distinct(long_soil$variable)} variables, {nrow(long_soil)} rows in {.path {long_soil_path}}.")
